theory.intro: Straight-line depreciation takes off the same **dollar amount** each period; declining balance takes off the same **percentage** of the current value. So one graph is a straight line and the other is a curve that flattens out.
facts: Straight-line uses $S = V_{0} - Dn$ and declining balance uses $S = V_{0}(1-r)^{n}$, both starting from the same $V_{0}$.
For a positive initial value and positive annual depreciation amount, straight-line loses the same amount every period and reaches zero at $n = V_{0}/D$. Use this valuation only while $S \geq 0$.
For a positive initial value and $0<r<1$, declining balance loses a percentage of a smaller amount each period, so its graph is a curve that never reaches zero at any finite time.
Both graphs meet at purchase. Depending on the depreciation amounts and rates, they may meet again after purchase, or the declining-balance value may be higher throughout.

For positive initial value, positive straight-line depreciation and $0<r<1$, if the declining-balance graph initially falls more steeply, the graphs cross once after purchase and declining balance is higher afterwards. Otherwise, declining balance is higher at every positive time within the straight-line model's nonnegative range.
To compare, work out both salvage values for the same $V_{0}$ and the same $n$, then say which is lower.
A method can change part-way through: work out the value at the changeover, then use it as the starting value for the second method.
steps: Work out the straight-line value with $S = V_{0} - Dn$.
Work out the declining-balance value with $S = V_{0}(1-r)^{n}$.
Compare the two values and answer the question asked.

foundation.question_text:
A van costs $\$30\,000$.
Find its value after $3$ years under straight-line depreciation of $\$4200$ per year, and under declining-balance depreciation at $12\%$ p.a.
Give money answers to the nearest cent.

A machine costs $\$44\,000$.
Straight-line depreciation removes $\$5500$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $20\%$ p.a.
Which method gives the **lower** salvage value after $4$ years, and what is it?
foundation.solution_text:
Straight-line:
$S = 44\,000 - 5500(4)$
$= \$22\,000$
Declining balance:
$S = 44\,000(0.8)^{4}$
$= \$18\,022.40$
The declining-balance method gives the lower salvage value, $\$18\,022.40$.

foundation.question_text:
A $\$12\,000$ asset depreciates at $30\%$ p.a. by the declining-balance method.
Explain why its value never reaches zero.
foundation.solution_text:
$S = 12\,000(0.7)^{n}$
For every value of $n$, $(0.7)^{n} > 0$, so $S > 0$.
Each year takes off $30\%$ of a smaller amount, so a fraction of the value always remains.

The two graphs cross once after purchase.
At $n = 5$ the straight line is still above the curve.
At $n = 6$ the straight line is below the curve.
The values are equal between $5$ and $6$ years.

foundation.question_text:
An asset costing $\$16\,000$ is depreciated either by $\$2600$ per year (straight-line) or at $25\%$ p.a. (declining balance).
Between which two whole years after purchase do the two methods give the same value?
foundation.solution_text:
Straight-line at $n = 4$: $16\,000 - 2600(4) = \$5600$
Declining balance at $n = 4$: $16\,000(0.75)^{4} = \$5062.50$
Straight-line at $n = 5$: $16\,000 - 2600(5) = \$3000$
Declining balance at $n = 5$: $16\,000(0.75)^{5} = \$3796.88$
The straight-line value drops below the declining-balance value between $4$ and $5$ years.

development.question_text:
An asset costs $\$25\,000$.
Find the annual amount of straight-line depreciation needed for it to be worth zero after $4$ years.

A car costing $\$50\,000$ is depreciated by $\$4000$ per year for $3$ years, after which the declining-balance method at $25\%$ p.a. is used.
Find its value $7$ years after purchase, to the nearest cent.

An asset costs $\$21\,000$.
Straight-line depreciation removes $\$1800$ per year; declining-balance depreciation is $10\%$ p.a.
Which method gives the **higher** value after $6$ years, and what is it?
Give the value to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
Straight-line:
$S = 21\,000 - 1800(6)$
$= \$10\,200$
Declining balance:
$S = 21\,000(0.9)^{6}$
$= \$11\,160.26$
The declining-balance method gives the higher value, $\$11\,160.26$.

development.question_text:
An asset costing $\$36\,000$ can be depreciated by $\$5000$ per year (straight-line) or at $22\%$ p.a. (declining balance).
Between which two whole years after purchase do the two methods give the same value?
development.solution_text:
At $n = 5$: straight-line $= 36\,000 - 5000(5) = \$11\,000$; declining balance $= 36\,000(0.78)^{5} = \$10\,393.83$
At $n = 6$: straight-line $= 36\,000 - 5000(6) = \$6000$; declining balance $= 36\,000(0.78)^{6} = \$8107.19$
The values are equal between $5$ and $6$ years.

development.question_text:
A machine costing $\$80\,000$ is depreciated by $\$9000$ per year using the straight-line method for $2$ years, after which the firm switches to declining-balance depreciation at $20\%$ p.a.
Find its value $5$ years after purchase.

mastery.question_text:
A council leases equipment valued at $\$70\,000$.
Method A is straight-line depreciation of $\$6800$ per year; Method B is declining-balance depreciation at $14\%$ p.a.
Under which method is the salvage value lower at the end of $4$ years?
Justify your answer with calculations.
Give money answers to the nearest cent.

An asset costs $\$54\,000$.
Straight-line depreciation writes it down to zero over $9$ years; declining-balance depreciation is $25\%$ p.a.
Between which two whole years after purchase do the two methods give the same value?
mastery.solution_text:
$D = \dfrac{54\,000}{9}$
$= \$6000$ per year
At $n = 8$: straight-line $= 54\,000 - 6000(8) = \$6000$; declining balance $= 54\,000(0.75)^{8} = \$5406.10$
At $n = 9$: straight-line $= 54\,000 - 6000(9) = \$0$; declining balance $= 54\,000(0.75)^{9} = \$4054.57$
The values are equal between $8$ and $9$ years.

mastery.question_text:
A business buys a press for $\$120\,000$.
It is depreciated by the straight-line method at $\$11\,000$ per year for $5$ years, after which the declining-balance method at $30\%$ p.a. is used.
Find the **total depreciation** at the end of $9$ years, to the nearest cent.
